objective: Make the native agent loop survive expected adversity: no run may end in fake success after a dropped model stream, ignored finish_reason, or cancellation; transient sampling failures replay in place; turn budget relays instead of failing; the per-task queue survives run failure and daemon restart; tool calls run behind an atomic idempotency fence and may execute in parallel.
end_state: All A00–A15 tasks landed with machine acceptance green: a TCP drop mid-stream either replays to a complete answer or fails the run visibly — never a truncated 'success'; max_tokens output continues once then degrades with an explicit marker; a 30+-turn task chains runs via InputKind::Continuation without user-visible error; a failed run does not stall the task queue and daemon restart reseeds undelivered inputs; cancellation produces run.cancelled with no completion proposal; oversized checkpoints truncate monotonically instead of failing silently; concurrent tool calls with the same operation key cannot double-execute and a failed effect leaves its key retryable.
non_goals: Context compaction engine (owned by project-context PRD FR-6; interface contract only)
Input-level failure redelivery (rejected in review R2; stream-level replay covers transients)
Execution-wave lease lifecycle defects in parallel.rs (DEC-2: separate workstream; registered as observation item 9 — do NOT fix here)
Codex harness route (ModelRoute::HarnessManaged bypasses the host broker)
Plugin process reuse / keep-alive across runs
Live token-by-token streaming to frontends (no channel exists; aggregated observations only)

agent_rules.anchor_resolution: Every file entry carries `anchors`: symbol names with line numbers AS OF 2026-10-02. Lines WILL drift as earlier tasks land. Resolve by SYMBOL NAME first (grep for the fn/const/enum), use the line number only as a hint. Never treat a stale line number as an error.
agent_rules.deviation_protocol: If an anchor symbol cannot be found: (1) git log -S '<symbol>' --oneline | head to see if it moved/renamed; (2) implement at the nearest semantically-equivalent location listed for the task; (3) append one line to docs/support/archive/prd/agent-loop-resilience/progress.md under Deviations describing old->new anchor. Do NOT stop, do NOT ask, do NOT redesign.
agent_rules.scope_freeze: Tasks implement exactly what their `what`/`description` say. Bugs found along the way that are NOT in this worklist get one line appended to progress.md under 'Found, not in scope' and are otherwise left untouched. Exception: a blocker that makes the task's own acceptance impossible -> implement the minimal fix and record it as a deviation.
agent_rules.decisions_final: DEC-1..DEC-4 are settled (see `decisions`). Their flip points are data/code locations, not re-openable questions. If implementation seems to conflict with a DEC, follow the DEC and record the tension in progress.md.
agent_rules.test_conventions: New integration tests live at the test_files path with #[tokio::test] / plain #[test] as appropriate, reusing `mod common;` for the A00 fixture inside r-code-runtime tests. Inline unit tests go in the same file's #[cfg(test)] module. Every acceptance_criteria entry maps to at least one named test; prefix test names with the task id (e.g. a02_incomplete_stream_returns_error_not_ok).
agent_rules.progress_tracking: After finishing each task: append to docs/support/archive/prd/agent-loop-resilience/progress.md — task id, status (done/partial), tests added (names), deviations (if any), and run `cargo test -p <pkg> --test <stem>` output summary (pass count). Partial is allowed only when a dependency task is itself partial.
agent_rules.vendor_policy: vendor/agent-contracts is a vendored fork already carrying local patches (see docs referencing deepseek-prefix-cache.md in code comments). Editing it in place is established practice; keep changes minimal and commented in the same style.

Implement in router host.checkpoint.save arm: (1) explicit MAX_CHECKPOINT_STATE_BYTES (const; set to 768KB aligned with the frame cap; document the coupling). (2) On exceed: HOST-side monotonic truncation — decode the state JSON, replace the OLDEST tool-result output_texts with placeholders (keep call id + first 200 chars + '[truncated by checkpoint budget]') until under bound, save the truncated payload once, journal a note event (e.g. checkpoint.truncated {bytesBefore, bytesAfter}); truncation is monotonic (never re-expands). (3) Still over after truncation (e.g. a single giant user message) -> loud RpcError with guidance. Host-side keeps the plugin oblivious and preserves append-only/prefix-cache discipline.
